hints: Integrate to logarithms, including the factors $1/4$ on the left and $1/2$ on the right.
Apply $x=0$ at $\theta=\pi/12$, using $\sin(\pi/6)=1/2$, to determine the constant.
Combine and exponentiate the logarithms, then isolate $x$ in terms of $\theta$.
walkthrough:
Separate variables in $\sin(2\theta)\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}\theta} = (4x + 3)\cos(2\theta)$ by dividing by $(4x + 3)\sin(2\theta)$ and multiplying by $\mathrm{d}\theta$:
$$\dfrac{1}{4x + 3}\,\mathrm{d}x = \dfrac{\cos(2\theta)}{\sin(2\theta)}\,\mathrm{d}\theta$$

Evaluate the constant $C$ using the initial condition $x = 0$ when $\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{12}$:
$$\text{At } \theta = \dfrac{\pi}{12}: \quad 2\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{6} \implies \sin(2\theta) = \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$$
$$\dfrac{1}{4}\ln(4(0) + 3) = \dfrac{1}{2}\ln\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) + C$$
$$\dfrac{1}{4}\ln 3 = -\dfrac{1}{2}\ln 2 + C$$
$$C = \dfrac{1}{4}\ln 3 + \dfrac{1}{2}\ln 2 = \dfrac{1}{4}\ln 3 + \dfrac{1}{4}\ln(2^2) = \dfrac{1}{4}\ln(3 \times 4) = \dfrac{1}{4}\ln 12$$

Substitute $C = \dfrac{1}{4}\ln 12$ back into the integrated equation:
$$\dfrac{1}{4}\ln(4x + 3) = \dfrac{1}{2}\ln(\sin(2\theta)) + \dfrac{1}{4}\ln 12$$

Exponentiate both sides to eliminate the logarithms:
$$4x + 3 = 12\sin^2(2\theta)$$
$$4x = 12\sin^2(2\theta) - 3$$
$$x = \dfrac{12\sin^2(2\theta) - 3}{4} = 3\sin^2(2\theta) - \dfrac{3}{4}$$
